newsitem.title: UK: P&O to take control of NSF in 25 mln stg deal.
newsitem.headline: P&O to take control of NSF in 25 mln stg deal.

text.p: P&O Plc said it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Royal Nedlloyd NV to buy Nedlloyd's 50 percent interest in North Sea Ferries (NSF) for 25.25 million stg, giving P&O 100 percent control.

It said in a statement that the acquisition was expected to generate savings of five million stg a year for P&O on a total cost basis for the NSF and Felixstowe, England operations of 140 million stg.
P&O said the savings would be achieved through job cuts of 100 by integrating the port functions in Europoort and Zeebrugge and reducing administrative staff.
There will also be associated savings in shore side costs.
NSF will be merged with P&O European Ferries and the new company will be called P&O North Sea Ferries.
P&O said the buy was a first move in "what is expected to be a major rationalisation of the UK ferry industry."
P&O and Nedlloyd announced plans to merge their container shipping business earlier this month.
P&O said on Tuesday the two companies "are not holding any further talks regarding any other parts of their business."
Completion is expected before November and will then be made retrospective to September 1.
NSF carried eight percent more passengers in the first six months of 1996 over a year ago and 14 percent more cars and six percent more freight, P&O said.
In 1995, NSF saw pretax profit of 4.3 million stg and it raised pretax profit in the first half of 1996 by 2.9 million stg over the same period of 1995.
It operates ten ships on four routes between the UK, the Netherlands and Belgium.

"Today's development achieves the twin aims of reducing costs by combining the NSF and Felixstowe operations and strengthening our position in the market," said P&O chairman Lord Sterling in a statement.
